agenda: The situation in the Middle East; Report of the Secretary-General on the United Nations Disengagement Observer Force (S/2025/784)
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: Our objective is a clean six-month renewal that preserves the 1974 Disengagement Agreement as the sole framework, underscores the inviolability of the area of separation, and supports UNDOF’s return to the Bravo side without politicized language. The main difficulty will be balancing generic references to violations and military activity so that the United States and other Council members can accept them, while ensuring the text does not single out any party and retains consensus. We will resist attempts to add one-sided condemnations or to condition UNDOF’s renewal on unrelated issues.

Replace “including military operations by any party” with “including military operations by any party, in particular by the Israel Defense Forces, and calls for the immediate withdrawal of Israeli forces from the area of separation;”

Add: “Demands that Israel immediately cease all military operations in the Syrian Arab Republic, withdraw its forces from the area of separation to the Alpha line, and fully respect the terms of the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement;”
After “ongoing military activity on the Bravo side of the area of separation,” add “as well as reports of Israeli military activity and violations in the area of separation,”

Guyana.change: Add a preambular paragraph: 'Condemning all violations of the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, including the continued unauthorized military presence and operations in the area of separation, and calling for the immediate withdrawal of all unauthorized forces from the area of separation and a return to the lines stipulated in the 1974 Agreement;'

After 'including military operations by any party', insert ', and calls for the immediate withdrawal of all unauthorized forces from the area of separation and full respect for the ceasefire line and the area of limitation;'

At the end of the paragraph, add: 'and to facilitate safe, unhindered humanitarian access to affected civilian populations in the area of operations, in accordance with international humanitarian law;'

Slovenia.change: Insert after 'prevent any breaches of the ceasefire and the area of separation': ', and to ensure the protection of civilians and full respect for international humanitarian law and international human rights law'.

After 'all violations of the Disengagement of Forces Agreement', add ', including on the protection of civilians, humanitarian access, and all violations and abuses of international humanitarian law and international human rights law'.

Somalia.change: Replace with: 'Reaffirming its strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, and reaffirming the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force;'

Add: 'Calls for the immediate withdrawal of all unauthorized military forces and equipment from the area of separation and the area of limitation to the positions existing before 8 December 2024, and for full respect for the ceasefire line;'

Add: 'Calls on all parties to take all feasible measures to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure and to ensure safe, unhindered and sustained humanitarian access to civilians in the area of separation and southern Syria;'

messages.Algeria: Algeria welcomes the deletion of the obsolete COVID-19 reference, the affirmation of Syrian sovereignty and territorial integrity, and the replacement of the outdated reference to the Syrian Arab Armed Forces. However, the text still fails to reflect the Secretary-General’s findings on Israeli military incursions and violations, which are central to the credibility of this Council. Algeria asks the penholders to incorporate the specific references and operative demand above; with these changes, we can support the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate.
messages.China: China supports the current draft as a balanced basis for renewing UNDOF's mandate and thanks the penholders for their efforts. We welcome the reaffirmation of Syria's sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity and the call for no military activity by any party in the area of separation. We urge all parties, including Israel, to respect the 1974 Disengagement Agreement, ensure UNDOF's safety and freedom of movement, and create conditions for UNDOF's return to its area of operations.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the renewal of UNDOF's mandate and believes the current draft provides a balanced basis for Council unity. We welcome the reaffirmation of Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity and the clear call on all parties to respect the 1974 Disengagement Agreement, the ceasefire and the area of separation. We also stress the need for unhindered freedom of movement and safety for UNDOF and Observer Group Golan personnel. Denmark has no changes to request at this stage.
messages.France: France supports the renewal of UNDOF's mandate and considers the draft a balanced text that reaffirms the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement and calls on all parties to respect the ceasefire line and the area of separation. We welcome the emphasis on UNDOF's safety, freedom of movement and impartiality, and encourage the Council to adopt the resolution by consensus.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the draft renewal of UNDOF as presented. We welcome the balanced reaffirmation of the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, Syrian sovereignty and territorial integrity, and the emphasis on UNDOF’s safety, security and freedom of movement. We encourage the Council to maintain consensus and stand ready to vote in favour of the text.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the renewal of UNDOF's mandate and welcomes the reaffirmation of Syria's sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity. We ask the penholders to strengthen the text by explicitly addressing unauthorized military presence in the area of separation and calling for withdrawal to the 1974 lines, rather than relying only on generic language. We also request a reference to safe and unhindered humanitarian access for affected civilians. These changes would reinforce the Council's commitment to the Disengagement Agreement and international law.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the draft as presented and is prepared to vote in favour of renewing UNDOF's mandate. We welcome the reaffirmation of the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic and the balanced call for no military activity in the area of separation by any party. We appreciate the emphasis on the safety and security of peacekeepers and on consultation with troop-contributing countries, and encourage the penholders to maintain Council unity on this technical renewal.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate as set out in the draft and appreciates the efforts of the co-penholders. We underline the obligation of all parties to fully respect the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, ensure the safety and freedom of movement of peacekeepers, and facilitate UNDOF’s return to its area of operations; the text is balanced and we can support it.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the draft as it stands and thanks the Russian Federation and the United States for their efforts to maintain Council unity. We welcome the text’s emphasis on UNDOF’s safety and security, its return to the area of operations, and performance and troop-contributing-country consultation; we see no need for changes at this stage and encourage consensus adoption.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the draft as circulated and believes it provides a balanced basis for renewing UNDOF’s mandate. We urge all parties to respect the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, ensure the safety and freedom of movement of peacekeepers, and maintain close consultation with troop-contributing countries.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia welcomes the balanced draft and strongly supports the renewal of UNDOF's mandate. We would like the text to more explicitly reflect the obligation of all parties to respect international humanitarian law and international human rights law and to protect civilians. We also request that the Secretary-General's reporting include information on protection of civilians, humanitarian access, and violations and abuses of international law, to strengthen accountability. We can support the draft with these adjustments.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the renewal of UNDOF's mandate and welcomes the draft's reaffirmation of Syrian sovereignty and territorial integrity. We ask the penholders to add language on the inadmissibility of acquiring territory by force, a clear call for withdrawal of unauthorized forces to pre-8 December 2024 positions, and a humanitarian access and civilian protection paragraph. These changes reflect Somalia's consistent positions and would strengthen the Council's message without delaying renewal.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the renewal of UNDOF's mandate for six months and welcomes the reaffirmation of Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as the clear reference to military operations by any party. We thank the penholders for a balanced and consensus-oriented text and can support it as drafted.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the current draft and thanks the Russian Federation for its penholdership. We welcome the six-month renewal of UNDOF’s mandate and the text’s emphasis on respecting the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, ensuring the safety and freedom of movement of peacekeepers, and supporting UNDOF’s return to its area of operations. We urge all parties to avoid military activity in the area of separation and call for the Council to adopt the resolution swiftly.

steps.summary: The revised draft incorporates generic, balanced language on violations, withdrawal of unauthorized forces, IHL and humanitarian access while avoiding explicit naming of Israel or a specific withdrawal date. It retains the six-month renewal and core UNDOF provisions, preserving Council unity and Russian co-penholder interests.

messages.Algeria: Algeria welcomes the incorporation of generic language on violations and withdrawal, which improves the text. However, the draft still avoids naming the Israel Defense Forces, whose incursions are central to the Secretary-General’s findings and to the credibility of this Council. We therefore request the two amendments above, and with them Algeria can support the renewal.
messages.China: China supports the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate and welcomes that the draft reaffirms Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, as well as the inadmissibility of acquiring territory by force. The text also appropriately calls for respecting the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, the ceasefire line and the area of separation, and for withdrawal of unauthorized forces. China has no further changes to request and will support the draft. We encourage all parties to ensure UNDOF’s safety, security and freedom of movement so that it can fully implement its mandate.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the revised draft and welcomes the balanced language on respect for the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, the withdrawal of unauthorized forces, and unimpeded humanitarian access. We appreciate the penholders’ efforts and can support renewal of UNDOF’s mandate until 30 June 2026. We encourage full implementation of UNDOF’s mandate, including force protection, performance, and the women, peace and security provisions.
messages.France: France supports the revised text and thanks the penholders for their efforts to produce a balanced draft. We welcome the strengthened language on respect for the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, the withdrawal of unauthorized forces, protection of civilians, and humanitarian access. France encourages all Council members to support the adoption of this resolution and to ensure its full implementation.
messages.Greece: Greece thanks the Russian Federation and the United States for their work on this draft. We support the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate and welcome the text’s clear reaffirmation of the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, the protection of civilians, and the safety and security of UN personnel. Greece will vote in favour of the current text.
messages.Guyana: Guyana thanks the penholders for incorporating key elements on condemnation of violations, unauthorized military presence, withdrawal from the area of separation, and humanitarian access. The text now reflects Guyana’s core concerns regarding sovereignty, territorial integrity, the inadmissibility of acquisition of territory by force, protection of civilians, and the safety of UNDOF personnel. Guyana supports the draft as a balanced basis for renewal and encourages all parties to comply fully with the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the draft as presented. It reflects key principles we have consistently upheld: Syria’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity, the inadmissibility of acquiring territory by force, and the need for all unauthorized forces to withdraw from the area of separation. We appreciate the penholder’s inclusive approach and urge the Council to maintain consensus in renewing UNDOF’s mandate.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the current draft and thanks the penholders for the inclusive text. It reflects Panama’s priorities: respect for Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, strict compliance with the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, protection of civilians and humanitarian access, and the safety and effectiveness of UNDOF. We encourage all Council members to unite behind the text for adoption.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the current text and thanks the penholders for incorporating key provisions on UNDOF’s mandate renewal, force protection, troop-contributing country consultation, and performance. We especially value the clear call for all parties to respect the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement and the emphasis on humanitarian access and civilian protection. We therefore do not request further changes and encourage the Council to adopt the resolution unanimously.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the revised draft and appreciates the inclusion of language on Syrian sovereignty, protection of civilians, and safe humanitarian access. The text also appropriately prioritizes UNDOF’s safety, mandate implementation, and full respect for the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. We therefore ask no further changes and encourage the Council to adopt the text by consensus.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia welcomes that our key requests on international humanitarian law, international human rights law, protection of civilians and expanded reporting have been incorporated into the revised text. The draft now contains the essential elements we have consistently advocated, including respect for the 1974 Agreement, withdrawal of unauthorized forces, protection of UN personnel and unimpeded humanitarian access. We therefore support the current text and encourage the Council to adopt it consensually.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the revised draft and welcomes the inclusion of our PP3 language and the humanitarian access provisions. Our remaining priority is an explicit call for the withdrawal of unauthorized forces to the positions existing before 8 December 2024, consistent with the 1974 lines and the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force. We ask the penholder to reflect this in OP2; it is important for us, though we would not block consensus if the generic 1974-lines formulation is retained.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate and welcomes the text’s balanced focus on all violations of the 1974 Disengagement Agreement, the protection of UN personnel and civilians, and humanitarian access. We appreciate the penholders’ efforts and can support the draft as it stands. We encourage all parties to respect the ceasefire line and area of separation and to facilitate UNDOF’s return to its area of operations.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports the renewal of UNDOF's mandate as drafted. We appreciate the balanced language that does not single out any party and emphasizes the importance of the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. We call on all parties to cooperate fully with UNDOF and to respect the ceasefire and the area of separation.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria has consistently supported UNDOF mandate renewals and the draft now includes stronger language on Syrian sovereignty, withdrawal of unauthorized forces, and violations, even if it does not single out Israel as requested. Algeria would vote yes while using the explanation to criticize the omission and reaffirm its position on Israeli occupation.
reasons.China: China has consistently supported UNDOF mandate renewals and was in support during the last negotiation round with no outstanding requests. The draft aligns with China’s emphasis on sovereignty, ceasefire compliance, and protection of UN peacekeepers.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark has consistently supported UNDOF mandate renewals and the draft reinforces respect for the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, UNDOF safety, civilian protection, and humanitarian access. Denmark made no requests in the last round and the penholder accepted its position, so no pre-vote explanation is necessary.
reasons.France: France supports the renewal of UNDOF and had already signalled support in the last negotiation round with no outstanding requests. The statement reflects France’s consistent position on Syrian sovereignty, respect for the 1974 Agreement, and protection of UN personnel and civilians.
reasons.Greece: Greece has consistently supported UNDOF mandate renewals and the draft broadly reinforces the 1974 Agreement, peacekeeper safety, and international law. The language is compatible with Greece’s support for Council unity and a rules-based settlement.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana has consistently supported UNDOF mandate renewals and the draft aligns with its emphasis on the 1974 Agreement, sovereignty, and civilian protection. It therefore votes in favour and explains its support before the vote.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan supported the draft during negotiations, and its provisions on Syrian sovereignty, ceasefire compliance, withdrawal of unauthorized forces, and peacekeeper safety align with Pakistan’s established positions. There is no basis to abstain or oppose.
reasons.Panama: Panama supports renewing UNDOF’s mandate and the draft’s emphasis on respecting the 1974 Disengagement Agreement, sovereignty, and protection of peacekeepers. Given its support and no outstanding requests, it does not need to speak before the vote.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea has consistently supported UNDOF mandate renewals and Council unity, and it prioritizes peacekeeping safety, respect for the 1974 Agreement, and protection of civilians. Voting in favour is consistent with its prior recorded votes and stated positions.
reasons.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation is the penholder and co-sponsor of the draft, which aligns with its support for Syrian sovereignty, the 1974 Disengagement Agreement, and UNDOF mandate renewal, so it votes in favour and explains its vote before the vote.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone has consistently supported UNDOF renewals and this draft aligns with its commitments to international law, UN peacekeeping, sovereignty, ceasefire compliance, civilian protection, and humanitarian access. It therefore votes in favour.
reasons.Slovenia: The draft renews UNDOF and includes language consistent with Slovenia’s consistent support for international law, territorial integrity, protection of civilians, and safety of peacekeepers. Slovenia therefore votes yes and explains its support before the vote.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia supports UNDOF’s mandate renewal and Syrian sovereignty, and its requested withdrawal language was partially reflected in OP2. It would thus vote in favour while explaining its interpretation of the withdrawal provision.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supported this text in the final negotiation round and has a longstanding policy of backing UNDOF mandate renewals and respect for the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. With no outstanding requests and broad Council support, the UK would vote in favour and would not need to take the floor before the vote.
reasons.United States of America: The United States is a co-sponsor of the draft and supported the prior UNDOF renewal consensus; the text is consistent with its stated support for UNDOF’s mandate and regional stability. Therefore the U.S. votes in favour and explains its support before the vote.

before.Algeria: Algeria will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The renewal of UNDOF’s mandate is essential for stability and for the protection of civilians and United Nations personnel in the area of operations. We welcome the text’s reaffirmation of Syrian sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force, and the clear call for the immediate withdrawal of unauthorized forces from the area of separation and the area of limitation. These are important and necessary elements. However, we regret that our request to explicitly name the Israel Defense Forces in the operative paragraphs was not retained. The Council cannot continue to address violations in an abstract manner when the Secretary-General’s report clearly documents Israeli military incursions and activities in the area of separation and in Syrian territory. Algeria’s support for this resolution does not diminish our firm position that the Israeli occupation must end and that all parties must respect the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. We will continue to insist that the Council uphold its responsibilities and reflect the realities on the ground without ambiguity or selective language.
before.China: China will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate so that the mission can continue to play its role in maintaining stability in the area of separation. We stress that the parties must respect the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, exercise maximum restraint, avoid any actions that endanger United Nations peacekeepers, and ensure the safety and security of UNDOF personnel. China also reaffirms the importance of respecting Syria’s sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity, and calls on all parties to work toward a comprehensive and durable political settlement.
before.France: France votes in favour of renewing UNDOF’s mandate. We welcome the Council’s unity in supporting the mission and reiterate the obligation of all parties to fully respect the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. France calls for the immediate withdrawal of all unauthorized forces from the area of separation, full respect for Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, the protection of civilians, and safe, unhindered humanitarian access.
before.Greece: Greece will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank the penholders for their efforts and reaffirm our full support for UNDOF and the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. All parties must respect the ceasefire line, the area of separation and the area of limitation, facilitate UNDOF’s operations and return, and ensure the safety of peacekeepers and civilians. Greece also underscores the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force and supports a just and durable settlement consistent with relevant Security Council resolutions.
before.Guyana: Mr. President, Guyana will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank the penholders for their efforts to renew the mandate of the United Nations Disengagement Observer Force, whose presence remains essential to stability in the region. We stress the obligation of all parties to respect the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, to cease unauthorized military activity in the area of separation, and to facilitate the safe and secure return of UNDOF personnel. We also underscore the need to protect civilians and ensure humanitarian access. Guyana remains committed to the sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity of Syria and to a just and durable peace based on the relevant Security Council resolutions.
before.Pakistan: Pakistan has consistently supported UNDOF’s mandate and the full implementation of the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. We remain deeply concerned by violations of the ceasefire and by any unauthorized military presence in the area of separation, which undermine Syrian sovereignty and regional stability. The draft addresses these concerns, including through its call for the withdrawal of unauthorized forces and the protection of civilians, while renewing UNDOF’s mandate and prioritizing the safety and security of peacekeepers. Pakistan therefore votes in favour.
before.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea will vote in favour of this resolution. We appreciate the penholders’ efforts to preserve Council unity on a matter that directly affects peacekeeping operations and regional stability. We underscore the obligation of all parties to respect the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, the ceasefire, and the inviolability of the area of separation. We also stress the need to ensure the safety and security of UNDOF personnel and to facilitate the mission’s return to its area of operations in accordance with its mandate. The Republic of Korea calls on all parties to exercise maximum restraint, protect civilians, and ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation will vote in favour of the draft resolution before the Council, which we have submitted together with the United States. The text is balanced and objective. It reaffirms the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force and the obligation of all parties to scrupulously respect the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. It condemns all violations, including unauthorized military presence in the area of separation, and calls for the immediate withdrawal of unauthorized forces and equipment to the lines stipulated in the 1974 Agreement. It also stresses the impartiality of UNDOF, the safety and security of peacekeepers and the need to ensure humanitarian access to affected civilians. We call on all parties to exercise maximum restraint, to avoid any steps that could escalate the situation and to cooperate fully with UNDOF. We support the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate for six months and the reporting requirements, including on violations, protection of civilians, humanitarian access and UNDOF’s return to its area of operations. We urge all Council members to support this text.
before.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone votes in favour of the draft resolution. We reaffirm our support for UNDOF’s mandate, the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, and the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. We call on all parties to respect the ceasefire, withdraw unauthorized forces from the area of separation, protect civilians, and ensure safe and unhindered humanitarian access. Renewing UNDOF’s mandate is essential to preserving stability and supporting a durable peace in the region.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We thank the penholders for their work. The renewal of UNDOF’s mandate is essential for stability in the region and for the safety and security of peacekeepers and civilians. Slovenia remains concerned by continued violations of the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, including military incursions and unauthorized military activity in the area of separation. We call on all parties to respect the ceasefire, the area of separation and the area of limitation, to withdraw unauthorized forces and equipment, and to fully comply with their obligations under international law, including international humanitarian law. We underscore the need for safe, unhindered humanitarian access and for the protection of United Nations personnel and premises. We reaffirm our commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of Syria and to the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force. We support UNDOF’s return to its area of operations as soon as conditions permit and encourage continued cooperation with the mission.
before.Somalia: Thank you, Mr. President. Somalia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We do so because the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate remains essential to preserving stability in the area of separation, protecting United Nations personnel, and supporting the full implementation of the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. Somalia reaffirms its strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic and to the principle of the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force. We welcome the strengthened language in operative paragraph 2 calling for the immediate withdrawal of all unauthorized military forces and equipment from the area of separation and the area of limitation to the positions stipulated in the 1974 Agreement. While we would have preferred an explicit reference to the positions existing before 8 December 2024, we interpret this provision as requiring the reversal of unauthorized changes on the ground and full respect for the ceasefire line. We call on all parties to exercise maximum restraint, protect civilians, facilitate humanitarian access, and ensure the safety and security of UNDOF personnel.
before.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States is pleased to join as a co-sponsor of this resolution and will vote in favour of renewing UNDOF’s mandate. UNDOF’s impartial presence and liaison role remain important to preventing further escalation between Israel and Syria and to supporting stability in the region. We call on all parties to respect the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, to avoid actions that endanger United Nations peacekeepers, and to ensure UNDOF’s safety, security, freedom of movement, and ability to implement its mandate. The United States also underscores the importance of protection of civilians and safe, unhindered humanitarian access. We thank the troop-contributing countries and UNDOF personnel for their service in a difficult environment.

after.Algeria:
Mr. President,

Algeria voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. We welcome the unanimous renewal of UNDOF’s mandate, which remains indispensable to stability in the area of operations and to the protection of civilians and United Nations personnel.

We also welcome the reaffirmation of the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force, and the call for the immediate withdrawal of unauthorized forces from the area of separation and the area of limitation.

At the same time, we regret that our request to explicitly name the Israel Defense Forces in the operative paragraphs was not retained. The Council cannot continue to address documented violations in an abstract manner. The Secretary-General’s report clearly records Israeli military activities and violations, and those realities must be reflected in the Council’s action and implementation.

The adoption of this resolution must now be translated into compliance by all parties with the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. All unauthorized forces must withdraw to the lines stipulated in that Agreement. The ceasefire must be respected, UNDOF’s safety, security and freedom of movement must be guaranteed, and safe and unhindered humanitarian access must be ensured.

Algeria will continue to follow the implementation of this mandate closely and will continue to insist that the Council address violations with clarity, consistency and accountability.
after.Denmark:
Mr. President, Denmark voted in favour of the resolution just adopted renewing the mandate of UNDOF. We welcome the Council’s unity and thank the penholders, the Russian Federation and the United States, for their efforts on a matter that is central to peacekeeping and regional stability.

UNDOF’s impartial presence and liaison role remain important to preventing escalation across the ceasefire line and supporting stability in the area of separation. Denmark reiterates the obligation of all parties to scrupulously respect the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, including the ceasefire line, the area of separation and the area of limitation. We remain concerned by continuing violations and call for the immediate withdrawal of all unauthorized forces and equipment to the positions stipulated in the 1974 Agreement.

We underline the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force and reaffirm our commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. All parties must ensure the safety, security and freedom of movement of UNDOF and United Nations personnel, facilitate the mission’s return to its area of operations as soon as practicable, protect civilians and allow safe, unhindered humanitarian access. Denmark will continue to support UNDOF’s mandate and the full implementation of the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement.
after.Panama: Mr. President, the Republic of Panama welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Disengagement Observer Force. Panama voted in favour because we believe that UNDOF’s impartial presence and liaison role remain essential to preventing escalation between Israel and Syria and to supporting full implementation of the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement. We reaffirm our commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic and to the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force. We call on all parties to scrupulously respect the ceasefire, the area of separation and the area of limitation, and to withdraw unauthorized forces and equipment to the lines stipulated in the 1974 Agreement. The safety and security of United Nations peacekeepers and civilians must be guaranteed, and UNDOF must be able to operate and return to its area of operations safely and securely. We also stress the need for safe, unhindered humanitarian access and full respect for international humanitarian law. Panama remains committed to the Council’s efforts to achieve a just, durable and comprehensive peace in the Middle East consistent with the relevant Security Council resolutions.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation voted in favour of the resolution just adopted and, as one of its penholders together with the United States, we welcome the Council’s unanimous support. The Security Council has today sent a clear and balanced signal in favour of UNDOF’s mandate, the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, and the sovereignty, independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic.

We note that the text reaffirms the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force, condemns all violations of the Disengagement Agreement and calls for the immediate withdrawal of unauthorized forces and equipment from the area of separation and the area of limitation to the lines stipulated in the 1974 Agreement. We proceed from the understanding that this applies to all unauthorized military presence, without exception. It is now essential that all parties respect the ceasefire, ensure the safety, security and freedom of movement of United Nations peacekeepers, and create conditions for UNDOF’s return to its area of operations.

The Russian Federation will continue to follow the implementation of this resolution closely and will work to prevent any escalation in the region and to support a just and durable settlement on the basis of the relevant Security Council resolutions.

Thank you.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Thank you, Mr. President.

The United Kingdom voted in favour of this resolution and welcomes the Council’s unanimous adoption of the renewal of UNDOF’s mandate. UNDOF’s impartial presence and liaison role remain essential to preventing escalation across the ceasefire line, and we pay tribute to its military and civilian personnel, including Observer Group Golan, and to the troop-contributing countries serving in a difficult environment.

The United Kingdom remains deeply concerned by violations of the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, including military activity and incursions in the area of separation and in Syrian territory. There should be no military forces, equipment, or personnel in the area of separation other than those of UNDOF. We call for the immediate withdrawal of all unauthorized forces and equipment to the lines stipulated in the 1974 Agreement, and for all parties to exercise maximum restraint, respect the ceasefire, and avoid any action that endangers United Nations peacekeepers.

We reaffirm our strong commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of Syria, and to the inadmissibility of the acquisition of territory by force. The United Kingdom’s position on the Golan Heights is unchanged: it is occupied territory, and we do not recognise Israel’s annexation. Israel has legitimate security concerns, but those must be addressed through the existing liaison arrangements and in full respect for the 1974 Agreement and international law.

We stress the need for UNDOF to have the safety, security, and freedom of movement required to implement its mandate, and we support its return to the Bravo side as soon as conditions permit. We also call on all actors in Syria to protect civilians, respect international humanitarian law, cease military actions in the UNDOF area of operations, and support an inclusive and credible political process in line with resolution 2254 (2015).

Thank you.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President. The United States welcomes the Council’s unanimous adoption of this resolution renewing the mandate of the United Nations Disengagement Observer Force. We were pleased to co-sponsor this text together with the Russian Federation, and we appreciate the constructive engagement of all Council members.

UNDOF’s impartial presence and liaison role remain important to preventing miscalculation and escalation between Israel and Syria. We call on all parties to respect the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement, to exercise maximum restraint, and to ensure the safety, security, freedom of movement, and unimpeded access of United Nations peacekeepers. The United States also underscores the importance of protecting civilians and ensuring safe, unhindered humanitarian access.

We thank the troop-contributing countries and all UNDOF personnel, including Observer Group Golan, for their service in a difficult environment. The United States will continue to support the stability of the region and the security of all parties consistent with our commitments and with the principles of the Charter.
